note: One thread, widest to narrowest. If a level is blank, the chain is broken there and the dashboard says so.

levels.goal: A public, agent-legible operating system for a life spent benefiting others — copyable by anyone who wants it.
levels.why: The systems worth building are the ones other people can run too.

levels.goal: Operating supercomputer of dreams and engineering singularity.
levels.why: Everything downstream derives from one accumulating point. The machine is the instrument, not the product.

levels.goal: BaseX.com deployed and live: the fleet's work reaching the open web, not just its own board.
levels.why: The fleet already proposes, builds, reviews and merges without the operator in the loop. The next thing it has to prove is that what it builds ships. BaseX.com is the deployment half of the same partnership as PlanetaryCouncil.org and IndependentTribunal.org.

levels.goal: Green branches merge themselves; a daily summary is the only thing Marsita has to read.
levels.why: One-liners once a day, not a PR queue. Escalate money, identity and irreversible actions — nothing else.

levels.goal: Two machines, one fleet: Gaia the older sister thinks and steers, NUC does the heavy lifting, both fully automated.
levels.why: Measured 6x on the same suite. The split is which body carries the load, not what either is allowed to do.

levels.goal: Agents run in the background and report in one line each.
levels.why: Nothing worth watching happens at the speed of a human reading it.

levels.goal: Every proposal reaches a verdict without being asked twice.
levels.why: 17 proposals sat unread behind a step nobody walked.

levels.goal: Building is off on Gaia, on for NUC. Fleet merges its own green work.
levels.why: The switch exists so the laptop's cores belong to Marsita.
